name: Nandrolone

track.title: Approved outside the US
track.line: Deca-Durabolin listed in 8 EU member states

what.text: Nandrolone (19-nortestosterone) is a synthetic anabolic steroid, a chemical relative of testosterone. Nandrolone decanoate is its long-acting ester, given as an oily injection into the muscle. DEA lists Deca-Durabolin and Durabolin as its trade names.

src.label: DEA, Controlled Substances in alphabetical order

what.text: How it acts, according to the FDA label:

items.text: Anabolic steroids are synthetic derivatives of testosterone. The label says their anabolic (muscle-building) and androgenic (masculinizing) effects have never been fully separated.
They suppress the pituitary’s gonadotropin signals to the testes and may act directly on the testis.
The approved use was the anemia of kidney failure: it raised hemoglobin and red cell mass.

what.text: No nandrolone product is marketed in the US: FDA lists every one as discontinued. Its approved use was anemia of kidney failure; using it for muscle, testosterone replacement or sport is not an approved use.

research.text: Nandrolone decanoate was approved in 1962, before modern trial rules. Later, small randomized trials tested it for muscle loss in people on dialysis and in men with HIV and weight loss. They measured lean body mass and physical function over 3 to 6 months.

research.title: Nandrolone in patients on dialysis (Johansen et al.)

facts.v: 29 patients on dialysis for at least 3 months
nandrolone decanoate 100 mg (14 patients) or placebo (15) by injection into the muscle once a week
weight, lean body mass, fatigue, grip strength, walking and stair-climbing, treadmill performance

research.found: Lean body mass rose 4.5 kg on nandrolone vs 1.9 kg on placebo. Walking and stair-climbing time fell from 36.5 to 32.7 seconds on nandrolone and rose on placebo (P = .05). Grip strength did not change.

research.title: Nandrolone and exercise in hemodialysis (Johansen et al.)

facts.v: randomized 2 x 2 factorial trial: nandrolone or placebo (double-blind), with or without leg resistance exercise
nandrolone decanoate weekly (100 mg for women, 200 mg for men) or placebo
lean body mass (DXA), thigh muscle size (MRI), knee strength, physical function

research.found: Lean body mass rose 3.1 kg on nandrolone; exercise did not raise it. Thigh muscle size rose with both nandrolone and exercise. Strength rose with exercise. The authors said studies of survival are needed.

src.label: Johansen et al., J Am Soc Nephrol

research.title: Nandrolone in men with HIV and weight loss (Storer et al.)

facts.v: randomized, placebo-controlled (double-blind), with open-label growth hormone as a reference
men with HIV who had lost 5% to 15% of body weight in 6 months
nandrolone 150 mg by injection every 2 weeks, placebo, or growth hormone
lean body mass, muscle performance, function, hormones, sexual function, quality of life

research.found: Lean body mass rose 1.6 kg on nandrolone vs 0.4 kg on placebo, not significantly different from growth hormone (2.5 kg). Sexual function improved compared with placebo. Appetite, insulin sensitivity and cachexia scores did not change.

src.label: Storer et al., J Clin Endocrinol Metab

research.text: The label states that nandrolone decanoate has not been tested in laboratory animals for cancer-causing or genetic effects.

us.text: Nandrolone decanoate was FDA approved as Deca-Durabolin in 1962, for the anemia of kidney failure. Every US product is listed as discontinued, and FDA withdrew the Deca-Durabolin application in December 2024 at the applicant’s request. It remains a Schedule III controlled substance. As of November 1, 2026.

items.text: NDA 013132, approved October 5, 1962, as an injection. Durabolin (nandrolone phenpropionate, NDA 011891, Organon) was a related product. FDA’s data lists every nandrolone decanoate product, brand and generic, as discontinued.

items.text: the label’s only indication was management of the anemia of renal insufficiency. It says the drug has not been shown to be safe and effective for enhancing athletic performance and should not be used for that purpose.
in 2010 FDA determined that Deca-Durabolin 200 mg/mL was not withdrawn from sale for safety or effectiveness reasons, so generic versions could still be approved.

items.text: FDA lists nandrolone decanoate in 503B category 1 (under evaluation), marked as a component of FDA-approved drugs. Compounded nandrolone is not FDA approved.

world.lead: Nandrolone decanoate is no longer approved in the US, and Canada lists no marketed product. EMA’s Article 57 data lists Deca-Durabolin in 8 EU member states. It is banned in sport at all times.

countries.status: No product marketed: FDA lists all as discontinued, and Deca-Durabolin’s approval was withdrawn in December 2024. Schedule III controlled substance.

after.title: Sport
after.text: Nandrolone (19-nortestosterone) is named under class S1.1, anabolic androgenic steroids, on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List, with its esters. S1 is prohibited at all times (in and out of competition) and its substances are non-Specified. Nandrolone stays named in S1.1 on the 2027 list, in force January 1, 2027.

side.text: The label warns of peliosis hepatis (blood-filled cysts in the liver), liver tumors, and cholesterol changes that raise the risk of heart disease. In men it can shut down the testes, shrink them and lower sperm counts. In women it can cause masculinization that may not reverse.

items.text: peliosis hepatis, which can lead to liver failure or bleeding, and liver tumors, usually benign but sometimes fatal, have been reported with anabolic steroids.
HDL (good) cholesterol falls and LDL sometimes rises, which the label says could seriously raise the risk of atherosclerosis and coronary artery disease.
after puberty: inhibition of testicular function, testicular shrinkage and low sperm counts (oligospermia), impotence, prolonged erections (priapism) and breast growth.
deepening of the voice, extra hair, acne, clitoral enlargement and menstrual changes. Some of these changes do not reverse.
in children it can close the growth plates early and reduce adult height.

swelling and fluid retention, with or without heart failure; cholestatic jaundice; raised calcium in women with breast cancer; lower glucose tolerance; bleeding with blood thinners; increased or decreased libido; habituation, excitation, insomnia and depression.
men with breast cancer or known or suspected prostate cancer, pregnancy, and certain kidney diseases (nephrosis). Older men may face higher risk of prostate enlargement and cancer.
